instruction: Open the Google Scholar profile of the corresponding author in Chrome browser.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('f11'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.scroll(-40)

metadata.explanation: Paraphrase of the original instruction. The corresponding author is Tianlin (Tim) Shi with Google Scholar ID qRAQ5BsAAAAJ. Task requires: (1) reading the PDF to identify the corresponding author, (2) searching for the author on Google Scholar, (3) navigating to their profile page. Evaluator verifies the URL contains both 'https://scholar.google.com/citations' and 'user=qRAQ5BsAAAAJ' using the existing is_expected_url_pattern_match metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (active_url_from_accessTree) correctly extracts the active tab URL from Chrome's accessibility tree
Metric (is_expected_url_pattern_match) correctly checks if URL contains all required patterns using regex search
Expected values are semantically correct: both 'https://scholar.google.com/citations' and 'user=qRAQ5BsAAAAJ' must be present in the URL
Coverage is complete: evaluator verifies the final URL matches the Google Scholar profile for the specific author (Tianlin Shi, ID: qRAQ5BsAAAAJ)
Data flow is correct: accessibility tree → URL extraction → pattern matching → verification result
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The expected patterns use plain strings instead of properly escaped regex patterns. While re.search() handles this correctly in practice, for strict regex correctness, special characters like '.', '/', ':' should be escaped (e.g., 'https://scholar\.google\.com/citations'). However, this does not affect functionality since the current patterns work correctly.
